questions.question: Baishakhi, the famous festival of Sikhs, is celebrated in which month every year?

__
 
• In India, **Baisakhi **marks the beginning of **spring**.
 
• Traditionally, **Baisakhi **marks the** end of the harvest season** and is a time of great joy and festivity for farmers.
 
• **Punjab and Haryana** are the states where the celebrations are concentrated.
 
• There are many names for this festival, including **Pohela Baishakhi in West Bengal**, **Bohag Bihu in Assam**, **Puthandu in Tamil Nadu**, **Phool Dei** **in Uttarakhand**, **Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka**, **Pooram Vishu in Kerala** and **Mahavishuva Sankranti in Odisha**.

• It is a festival in Rajasthan. There is a celebration of spring and harvest.

• Traditionally held in Maharashtra. God Ganesh is revered during this ten-day festival.
 
 
 
• **Yaosang**
 
 
• People from diverse communities gather in Manipur to celebrate this festival.

questions.question: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of land, which of the following land was known as gifted to temples?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Devadana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Chola inscriptions**

__
 
• The funds from the revenues were used to keep the king's army afloat as well as to build temples and forts. The authority of collecting revenue was from powerful families.
 
• The Brahmanas were often honoured by kings with land gifts. These grants were written down on copper plates and distributed to the people who were given the land.
 
• **The Chola inscriptions cited various types of land:**
 
 
• **Brahmadeya **- The lands gifted to Brahamanas.
 
• **Vellanvagai **- Land of non-Brahamana peasant owners.
 
• **Shalabhoga **- The lands for the maintenance of a school.
 
• **Devadana** - Land gifted to temples
 
• **Pallichchhandam **- Land donated to Jaina organisations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayalaya **(850–871 CE) overthrew the Kaveri delta from Muttaraiyar. He built the city of **Thanjavur **and established the Chola kingdom in 850.
 
• **Rajaraja I** was regarded as the most powerful Chola ruler.
 
• The well-known dancing figure of Shiva as Nataraja fully developed during the Chola Period
 
• The Grand Temple of Tanjavur, known as **Rajarajisvaram **and **Brihadishvarar Temple**, were some of the outstanding examples of Chola architecture, painting, sculpture and iconography.

questions.question: How many times did India organise the Commonwealth Games?

questions.question: Identify a dark-coloured amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**Humus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humus **is an amorphous dark-coloured and colloidal substance which is highly resistant to microbial action.
 
• It undergoes decomposition at an **extremely slow rate**.
 
• It can also act as a **bank for nutrients**.
 
• The process that leads to the formation of humus is known as **humification**.
 
• Humus is further degraded by some microbes and the release of inorganic nutrients occurs through the process known as mineralisation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afd4ca090623bda7f7acfd92b998278a745c773f8d0360f601d8e070d8038404.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chitin**

 
 
• Chitin is the most abundant amino polysaccharide polymer occurring in nature and is the building material that gives strength to the exoskeletons of crustaceans, insects, and the cell walls of fungi.
 
 
 
• **Carotenoids**
 
 
• They are pigments in plants, algae, and photosynthetic bacteria. These pigments produce bright yellow, red, and orange colours in plants, vegetables, and fruits.
 
• Carotenoids act as a type of antioxidant for humans.
 
 
 
• Colloids
 
 
• A colloid is one of the three primary types of mixtures, with the other two being a solution and suspension. A colloid is a mixture that has particles ranging between 1 and 1000 nanometers in diameter, yet are still able to remain evenly distributed throughout the solution.

questions.question: A Hindu festival celebrated by the Tamil community that falls in the Tamil Solar Month is called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thaipusam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thaipusam** is an important festival celebrated by the Hindus of southern India during the Tamil month of Thai (January - February). Outside of India, it is observed mainly by the Tamil-speaking community settled in Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, Sri Lanka and elsewhere around the world.
 
• Thaipusam is devoted to the Hindu god **Murugan**, the son of Shiva and Parvati.
 
• **Murugan **is also known as **Karttikeya**, **Subrahmanya**, Shadanana, Skanda and Guha.
 
• It is believed that on this day, Goddess Parvati offered a lance to Lord Murugan to defeat the demon army of Tarakasura and combat their evil deeds. Therefore, Thaipusam is a celebration of the victory of good over evil.
 
• In **Singapore**, the festival is celebrated with a chariot procession that begins at the **Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple **at 397 Serangoon Road in the Little India district.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karaga**

 
 
• The Karaga festival is held at the **Dharmaraya Swamy Temple** in **Bangalore**.
 
• During Mahabharata, Draupadi, wife of five Pandavas made several Veera Kumaras (brave sons) to form a mini army and conquer the demon Timirasura. At the time of her death, these Veera Kumaras begged Draupadi not to leave them. Draupadi instead promised to return each year during the full moon day of Chaitra masa (month). Karaga festival is celebrated each year to mark the return of Draupadi in the form of Adishakti.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**
 
 
• It is the soul of **Assam **and is celebrated across the state with enormous zeal and enthusiasm.
 
• There are **three Bihu** festivals namely ‘**Bohag Bihu**’ celebrated in the month of ‘Bohag’ (Baisakh, the middle of **April**), ‘**Magh Bihu**’ observed in the month of ‘Magh’ (the middle of **January**), and **‘Kati Bihu**’ celebrated in the month of ‘Kati’ (Kartik, the middle of **October**).
 
 
 
• **Onam**
 
 
• The festival of Onam is celebrated all over the state of Kerala. Kerala during Onam is marked by happiness, excitement and enjoyment among all sections of people.
 
• Onam is marked as an outcome of reasons that have to do with mythology as well as old agrarian practices.

questions.question: Goods and services tax (GST) became operational from __ __.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 July 2017.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​GST was passed as the 101st Amendment Act of 2016.
 
• GST__ __(__Goods and Services Tax): is a comprehensive indirect tax on the manufacture, sale and consumption of goods and services throughout India.
 
• The four basic rate structures of GST are 5%. 12%, 18% and 28%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• The motto of GST - is "One Nation, One Tax, One Market".
 
• Three types of taxes in Indian GST are State GST(SGST)/ Union Territory GST(UTGST), Central GST(CGST) and Integrated GST(IGST).
 
• GST bill was passed by Rajya Sabha on 3rd August 2016.
 
• GST bill was passed by Lok Sabha on 8th August 2016.
 
• GST bill was signed by President on 8th September 2016.
 
• GST came into effect from 1st July 2017.
 
• Articles deals with the formation of the GST council is 279A.
 
• The Chairman of the GST council is Union Finance Minister.
 
• The first Chairman of the GST council is Arun Jaitley. 
 
• The concept of GST was first presented in Parliament by P. Chidambaram in 2005. 
 
• India has chosen the Canadian model of dual GST. 
 
• The first country to introduce GST: France in 1954.

• **Nagaram **- Where merchants and traders resided

questions.question: What is the average height of troposphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Troposphere

__
 
• The lowermost layer of the atmosphere with an average height of 13 km (18 km over the equator and 8 km over the poles).
 
• The air we breathe exists here. Almost all the weather phenomena (like rainfall, fog, clouds, dew, frost and hailstorm) occur in this layer.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height at the rate of 6.5℃ per 1000m. This is called normal lapse rate.
 
• The height of the troposphere varies from the equator towards the pole (decreases towards the poles) and from one season to another (increases during summer while decreases during winter) during a year.
 
• The upper limit is called the tropopause which is 1.5 km thick. (The word “troposphere” literally means “zone/region of mixing” and tropopause means “where the mixing stops”).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Stratosphere

 
• Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere. It extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomenon, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains a layer of ozone gas between the height of 15 to 30 km (also called Ozonosphere).
 
• Temperature increases with height due to the absorption of UV rays by the ozone layer.
 
• The upper limit of the stratosphere is known as stratopause.

Mesosphere

 
• Lying above the stratosphere this is the third layer of the atmosphere and extends between 50 km and 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height again.
 
• The uppermost limit is the mesopause where the temperature becomes -80℃.

Thermosphere

 
• Temperature here rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The International Space Station is situated in this layer.
 
• It is further divided into two layers:

Ionosphere:

 
• It extends between 80 - 400 km.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission. In fact, radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• Includes a number of ionic layers with increasing heights like the D layer, E layer, F layer and G layer.

Exosphere:

 
• This is the upper most layer of the atmosphere.
 
• This layer has very thin air.
 
• Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.
 
• The density here is very low and the atmosphere resembles a nebula because it is highly rarefied.

9c

questions.question: pH of milk of magnesia is __ __ .

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Acid substances usually produce a sour taste.
 
 
• The pH value of the Bases are greater than 7 (7 to 14)

• The pH value of the neutral substance is equal to 7.
 
• The pH value of the pure water is 7.

questions.question: The real executive power is vested in the Council of Ministers with the ________ as its head.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Real executive power vests in a Council of Minister with the Prime Minister as the head.
 
• Article 74(1) of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the House of the People.
 
• Thus, it is clear that the real executive power under the Constitution of India rests with the Prime Minister and his council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the states, the Governor, as the representative of the President, is the head of the Executive, but real executive power rests with the Chief Minister who heads the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Council of Ministers of a state is collectively responsible to the elected legislative assembly of the state.
 
• The Constitution governs the sharing of legislative power between Parliament and the State Legislatures and provides for the vesting of residual powers in Parliament.
 
• The power to amend the Constitution also vests in Parliament.
 
• The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President and Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.

questions.question: What is the numerical value of a physical quantity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnitude.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **measurement or absolute value** of a quantity is its **magnitude**.
 
• A magnitude is represented by a** positive real number.**
 
• The **magnitude of positive numbers** is equal to their **own magnitude.**
 
• The** magnitude of a negative number** is its absolute value or the negative number without the **minus sign.**
 
• The magnitude of a **complex number** is its **modulus.**
 
• A **scalar quantity's numerical **measure in some unit is referred to as its magnitude.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reference:**

 
 
• A relationship between objects known as a reference occurs when **one object designates**, provides a connection to, or** links** to, another object.
 
 
 
• **Direction:**
 
 
• **​**The term "direction" is frequently used to describe the way **something is travelling or pointing.**
 
 
 
• **Distance:**
 
 
• **​**Distance is a measurement of **how far apart **two things or points are, either **numerically or occasionally qualitatively.**

questions.question: In 1849, the Paramhans Mandali was established to work for the abolition of ‘Caste’ at __ __.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1849,** a** covert socio-religious organization** called the **Paramhans Mandali **was founded in **Bombay.**
 
• It shared a close relationship with **Manav Dharma Sabha**, which was established in **Surat in 1844.**
 
• **Dadoba Pandurang, Durgaram Mehtaji,** and several of his friends founded it
 
• It served as a **covert organization,** and it's thought that when its existence was made public in** 1860, it quickly disintegrated.**
 
• It was the first socioreligious **institution in Maharashtra.**
 
• This Mandli's founders held a** monotheistic belief.**
 
• They were mostly concerned with** disobeying caste laws.**
 
• The members consumed **food prepared** by members of** lower castes **during their sessions.
 
• Also, the Mandala **advocated women's education** and **widow remarriage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Manav Dharma Sabha:

 
 
• One of the oldest organizations for **socio-religious change** in **Gujarat and British India** was the Manav Dharma Sabha.
 
• **Durgaram Manchharam Mehta, Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar,** and a few others founded it on **June 22, 1844 in Surat.**
 
• Exposing the hypocritical practices seen in the** Christian, Muslim, and Hindu religions** was one of the Sabha's main objectives.
 
• As** Dadoba and Durgaram **departed for **Bombay in 1846 **and** Rajkot in 1852, **respectively, it ceased to exist.​

questions.question: In football, when the ball strikes the frame of the goal or the referee and remains within the goal and touch lines, it is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**still in play.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If, for any reason, the ball strikes the frame of the goal or the referee and remains within the goal and touch lines,** it is still in play**. A goal is scored when the entire ball has crossed the goal line within the frame of the goal.
 
• A** challenge or tackle** that **threatens **an opponent's **safety **or makes use of **excessive force or brutality **must be penalized as **serious foul play.**
 
• Serious foul play is committed by any player who lunges at an opponent while vying for the b**all from the front, the side, or the back, using one or both legs, with excessive force, **or while putting the opponent's safety in peril.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The ball is** out of play** when it has **wholly passed over the goal line** or touchline on the ground or in the air play has been stopped by the** referee** it** touches a match official**, remains on the field of play and a team starts a **promising attack** or the ball goes **directly into the goal** or the team in** possession** of the ball changes in all these cases, play is restarted with a** dropped ball.**
 
• **Ball in play**
 
 
• The ball is in play at all other times when it touches **a match official** and when it **rebounds off a goalpost, crossbar or corner flagpost** and remains on the field of play.

questions.question: 'Modernisation’ as a goal of planning in context of the Indian economy was NOT aimed at:

options.text: increase in production of goods and services

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**adopting a Western lifestyle.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Modernization **is the **adoption of cutting-edge technology **in the production sector and a **shift in social values**.
 
• Modernization, therefore, involves** two main components:**
 
• **Adoption of new technology:**
 
 
• It** boosts efficiency** and productivity.
 
• For instance**, utilizing HYV (high-yielding variety) seeds** and** new agricultural tools i**nstead of outdated ones can boost agricultural production.
 
• Similar to this, an industry can boost production by **installing additional machines** in its manufacturing facility.
 
 
 
• **Changes in social attitudes** also have a significant impact.
 
 
• For instance, acceptance of **contraceptive methods** aids in reducing population increase.
 
• Equal rights and** pay for men and women** will also promote the best possible use of **women's talent.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **economic plan **allots a **country's resources** to accomplish the broad and **detailed objectives** that the government has set for it over a given time period.
 
• These plans are called as **"five-year plans"** in India since they are developed for a period of five years.
 
• In **1950, the Planning Commission** was established with **Jawaharlal Nehru **as its chairman.
 
• It identified the kind of plan best suited for** accelerating economic growth.**
 
• **The Prime Minister of India **serves as the Planning Commission's chair.
 
• **Functions**:
 
 
• Evaluation of the material, financial, and human
 
• creation of a strategy to maximize their effectiveness and balance
 
• distribution of resources and the setting of priorities.

questions.question: In 1664, who discovered the fifth star in the Trapezium, an asterism (mini-constellation) in the constellation Orion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Englishman Robert Hooke** was a **polymath** who worked as an** architect, scientist, and natural philosopher.**
 
• He is recognized with being one of two scientists to use a** compound microscope **he created himself to** discover microbes in 1665.**
 
• Hooke devoted a lot of time to **unraveling the universe's secrets.**
 
• The** Big Red Spot of Jupiter **was first noted by Hooke, who also confirmed the **planet's rotation.**
 
• The **fifth star in the Trapezium, an asterism** in the constellation Orion, was found by **Hooke in 1664.**
 
• Hooke's **meticulous depictions of Mars** from 1666 made it possible to determine the** planet's rotational period **more than 200 years later.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **George Willis Ritchey:**

 
 
• **American astronomer, telescope manufacturer, and opticia**n George Willis Ritchey was born in Tuppers Plains, Ohio.
 
• Along with Henri Chrétien, he designed th**e Ritchey-Chrétien reflecting telescope.**
 
 
 
• **Giordano Bruno:**
 
 
• Italian philosopher Giordano Bruno was also a** mathematician, poet, cosmological thinker, and practitioner of the Hermetic esoteric.**
 
• His** cosmological theories**, which conceptually included the then**-novel Copernican paradigm,** are well recognized.
 
 
 
• **Johannes Kepler:**
 
 
• **German astronomer, mathematician, astrologer, natural philosopher, and composer** Johannes Kepler also wrote about music.
 
• He played a significant role in the **Scientific Revolution **of the **17th century** and is best remembered for his laws of** planetary motion. **
